goal: Implement and verify the smallest useful Codex capability-supervisor layer above CGKN librarian context while preserving the reviewed Provider and delivery contracts.
acceptance_criteria: The supervisor consumes only a bounded, hashed escalation request derived from librarian context and evidence references.
The validated response is advisory and cannot claim formal PASS, write a sealed generated candidate, package, or deliver.
The retained support pipeline orders context support before the supervisor and makes the validated brief available to later workers through existing agent_session and whiteboard communication.
A project-local Codex skill describes the role and passes the skill validator.
An offline replay of the failed FocusForge CLI run returns actionable bounded guidance without an API credential or external request.
Applicable kernel, schema, pipeline, management, and focused regression tests pass.

quality_metrics.measure: bounded Codex escalation usefulness and authority isolation
quality_metrics.target: request and response remain bounded and hashed, produce actionable guidance, and reject formal evidence or delivery claims
quality_metrics.method: contract tests and offline failed-generation replay

quality_metrics.target: no new Codex conversation generation route or delivery exit

quality_metrics.method: pytest targeted profile and skill validation

prevention: Use EXP-CGKN-LIBRARIAN-001 to bound the escalation packet instead of copying full run context.
Use EXP-CGKN-QUALITY-001 to keep advisory guidance separate from implementation, evidence, packaging, and delivery truth.
Define prohibited response fields and actions before implementation.
assurance: Review schema, skill, kernel, and support-pipeline authority boundaries.
Verify that only referenced evidence is selected and secrets are redacted.
control: Run schema and deterministic contract tests.
Run an offline replay using preserved failed Provider evidence.
Run kernel, support-pipeline, skill, and project-management regressions.
improvement: Measure whether one supervisor brief reduces Provider request count on a later user-authorized capped generation run.

interface_expectations: The librarian remains the context-selection owner; Codex receives only its bounded projection plus explicit failure evidence.
Codex returns a validated support response through agent_session and bounded whiteboard fields.
Provider output validation, post-build finalization, local_packager, public_delivery_gate, and delivery_manifest remain unchanged authorities.

feedback: The bounded request, sealed Codex response, validated capability brief, agent_session events, and whiteboard projection completed against the preserved FocusForge failure evidence with zero external API calls.
Schemas, authority rejection tests, direct CLI handoff, skill validation, support-pipeline behavior, kernel guards, formal Provider regressions, and management validation passed.
The retained support pipeline declares the Codex role but refuses Provider or local-model impersonation when an external Codex handoff is absent.
Automatic background creation of a new Codex task is not included in this increment, and Provider-call reduction remains unmeasured until a later user-authorized capped live generation.

worked: The prior failed run compressed into a 5439-byte request and a 4273-byte validated brief without copying the 313509-byte phase log or 133174-byte Tests librarian index.
Explicit negative authority fields, strict schemas, hashes, and prohibited-key checks kept the powerful external role advisory and auditable.
Project-level AGENTS instructions and a validated skill make the role reusable by later Codex sessions in this repository.
did_not_work: The first direct CLI replay exposed a script-import-path defect when appending agent_session; the root and scripts paths were then made explicit and covered by a subprocess regression test.
The installed Windows Codex executable was not directly launchable from this shell, so autonomous task creation was intentionally not made part of the support pipeline.
experiments: On the next authorized live generation, enforce a fixed Provider-request ceiling and compare first-pass goal fidelity and request count with and without one validated Codex capability brief.
